title: When the Vector Falls Anew
premise: Hazel Yarrow, navigator of the salvage hauler Perihelion, has spent years tending a navigation beacon whose commissioning records were erased — and quietly maintaining the cryo-bay holding two hundred sleepers from a war nobody will discuss. When a distress signal arrives in dead Old Meridian, Hazel discovers she can read it fluently: she is herself a copy, decanted from one of the sleepers. The signal's senders are the sleepers' original faction, demanding their people be woken before the rival faction's descendants aboard the ship can stop it. In the climax, Hazel wakes the sleepers against orders, forcing both halves of humanity to confront the war that split them; the resolution sees the crew and the revived colonists forge an uneasy found family, with Hazel choosing to remain the bridge between them rather than learn which memory of her original life was real.
about_author: S. M. Halloran is a former maritime radio operator who turned to science fiction after a decade of listening to voices arrive out of nowhere across empty water. They write about people who keep machines running long after everyone else has forgotten why.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Hazel performs her lonely maintenance shift on the unregistered beacon while the Perihelion's small crew sleeps, establishing her ritual care for the mysterious cryo-hold. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: quiet devotion masking loneliness; she talks to the sleepers like family she's never met.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: A distress signal arrives in Old Meridian, a language extinct two centuries. Hazel understands it instantly and hides this from Captain Okafor. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: uncanny dread — her fluency feels less like skill than memory.

chapters.title: Crew Manifest, Redacted
chapters.summary: Engineer Teodoru helps Hazel dig into ship archives, finding the beacon's records scrubbed and the cryo-bay absent from every official manifest. POV: alternating Hazel/Teodoru. Emotional beat: growing conspiracy; the first spark of found-family loyalty between the two outsiders.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel enters cryo-bay maintenance and finds her own face on sleeper 114. A hidden log confirms she was decanted from the hold eleven years ago. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: identity collapse — everything she remembers may be inherited, not lived.

chapters.title: Okafor's Silence
chapters.summary: Captain Okafor reveals she has always known: the Perihelion is a custody ship, and waking the sleepers is forbidden by treaty with the faction that won the old war. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: betrayed trust reframed as protection; loyalty vs. truth sharpens.

chapters.title: The Signal Answers Back
chapters.summary: The distress sender — a surviving colony ship of the losing faction — locks onto the beacon and demands its people or threatens to fire. The crew must choose sides. POV: Teodoru. Emotional beat: external pressure crystallizes internal divisions; Teodoru pledges himself to Hazel despite the risk.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Heartbeats
chapters.summary: Hazel secretly begins the revival sequence, one sleeper at a time, while Okafor races to negotiate a standoff. The first awakened sleeper recognizes Hazel's voice but calls her by another name. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: awe and grief entwined — she meets her origin and loses her certainty in the same hour.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Small Hours
chapters.summary: Okafor attempts to shut down the revival; Teodoru and the partially awakened sleepers stand with Hazel. The hostile colony ship opens fire on the beacon. POV: Okafor. Emotional beat: the captain's crisis — enforcing a lie to keep peace, or breaking faith to tell the truth.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Climax: with the beacon failing, Hazel broadcasts the full unredacted history of the war to both ships, then completes the revival of all sleepers, forcing both factions' descendants to face each other unarmed by ignorance. The colony ship stands down. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: costly courage — truth nearly kills them all, and saves them anyway.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Resolution: the merged crews bury the treaty, recommission the beacon openly as a memorial, and chart a shared course home. Hazel declines genetic testing that would reveal which memories are hers, choosing the family she's made over the past she lost. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — identity as choice, not inheritance.
